sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Anjeet Singh,Kamlesh Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Raj Narayan Singh Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. In compliance of order of this Court, original ossification test report of the victim has been received which indicates her age to be 17 years.

3. The original ossification test report of the victim shall be returned to the office of C.M.O.
concerned after retaining photostat copy of the same on record.

4. Heard Sri Anjeet Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Raj Narayan Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

sentences.text:
5. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.309 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376(3) I.P.C. and 4(2)
POCSO Act, Police Station- Karwi Kotwali Nagar, District- Chitrakoot, during the pendency of trial.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the victim is a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded U/s 164 Cr.P.C.

The victim by her looks seems to be major,
although she is stated to be 17 years old as per the ossification test report, as such, a leverage of two years may be granted to the applicant on the upper side.
8. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no medical corroboration of the incident.
There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 25.5.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
9. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

10. The Supreme Court in Jaya Mala vs. State of J & K, (1982) 2 SCC 538 and Mohd. Imran Khan vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2011) 10 SCC 192 has opined that the radiologist cannot predict the correct date of birth rather there is a long margin of 1 to 2 years on either side.

sentences.text: 11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the statement of the victim recorded U/s 164 Cr.P.C. and there being no medical corroboration of the incident, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Sunil @ Sushil, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

14. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
